JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 05.10.2024.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 05.10.2024 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding by riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-04- JT-4077 on Bengaluru- Nelamangala NH-48 service road, while so proceeding near TCI ETO lorry parking, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru,
at that time the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 came in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Abhay Vasishta Hospital,
Madanayakanahalli, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 20 years, working at Private Company, and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner lost his job and income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1-owner has not appeared before the tribunal,
hence placed exparte.
After service of summons, the respondent No.2- insurance company has appeared through its counsel, and filed written statement.

The respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of GCV Public carrier other than 3 wheeler Package policy bearing No.2230003123 P109825897 in favour of first respondent in respect of New Bharth Benz having Engine and Chassis bearing No.926956D0158527 & MEC826CKPP151401 which is valid from 10.11.2023 to 09.11.2024 and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further it has contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

Further contended that, there Aravind M vs Sunstar Logistics Pvt Ltd on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6476587/
2 is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

sentences.text: It has denied the age, occupation, income of the petitioner.
Accordingly this respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Lorry bearing Reg. No. HR-55-AR- 4649 by its driver, in RTA took place on 05.10.2024 at about 8.30 p.m on Bengalur-Nelamangala NH-48 Service Road, near TCI ETO Lorry Parking?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
Further examined Dr. Ramesh B., Orthopaedic surgeon as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P14 & 15.
On the other hand the respondent has not led any rebuttal evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, IMV notice and reply,
wound certificate and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Manjula N. who is the mother of the petitioner.
In the Ex.P1 & P2 they have alleged the negligence of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649.
In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P3.
On perusal of Ex.P3 the accident spot is in the left side of the road in which the petitioner was proceeding.
This shows that the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 being negligent came to his extreme left side and caused the accident.

10. The Ex.P4 is the IMV report wherein the motor cycle bearing No. KA.04.JT.4077 in which the petitioner was proceeding has got damages in its handle bar left side, electrical wiring, crash guard Aravind M vs Sunstar Logistics Pvt Ltd on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6476587/
3 left side, switcher box.
On the other hand, the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR- 4649 has got damages in its front bumper left side.
This shows the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.
No.HR-55-AR- 4649 changed his lane towards the left side without observing the other vehicles proceeding in its left side.
The driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 not examined before this tribunal by denying his negligence.
The petitioner being the victim eyewitness deposed about the negligence of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649.
On the other hand, the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 being the eyewitness proper person to deny his negligence.
But the said driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 not examined before this tribunal.

11. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 and produced documents in support of his case to prove the alleged negligence.
The PW.1 was cross-examined at length by denying the negligence of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55- AR-4649 but nothing been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Thus, it can be concluded that, the main negligence is on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 who caused the accident.

12. Ex.P8 charge sheet was also came to be filed against the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.
No.HR-55-AR- 4649.
The IO has opined that the negligence was on the part of driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR- 4649.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner and also to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.
13. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649.
Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the negligent act of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649.
14. The respondent No.2 even though filed written statement has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.

The charge sheet was came to be filed on the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649 for the offences punishable under Sec. 281,
125(b) of The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023.

Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the negligent act of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR-4649.

sentences.text: In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

17. Further it is contended by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company that there is inordinate delay in registering the FIR, as such the case of the petitioner has to be looked suspiciously.
In this regard if we perused Ex.P.2 complaint it shows that as the petitioner was under the treatment they were unable to give the complaint soon after the accident.
Further Ex.P.11 discharge summary, Ex.P.7 wound certificate also discloses that the petitioner admitted to their hospital on 05.10.2024 by alleging the history of RTA.
The contents of Ex.P.11 and P.7 supported the case of the petitioner that the delay is due to the genuine reasons.

18. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondents made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
The respondents have not led any rebuttal evidence.
19. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 05.10.2024 which was caused by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR- 4649 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
20.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 20 years.
As per DL and Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P9 & 10 the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 18.01.2004.
The accident was took place on 05.10.2024.
Hence as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 20 years.

sentences.text: According to the petitioner he was working at Private company and suffered multiple fractures.
The photograph produced at the time of arguments shows the present condition of the petitioner.
The evidence available before this tribunal shows that the petitioner sustained femur and tibia fracture in left leg and femur fracture with crush injury in the left leg.
The evidence of PW2 doctor shows that the petitioner walking with some external support.
The disability caused to the petitioner certainly affect on his occupation to greater extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 25% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,500 X 12 X 18 X 25% =Rs.8,91,000/- which is the total loss of future income.
d) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P11 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 31 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.35,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
e) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 31 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

By considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.31,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 31 days in the hospital.
f) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The petitioner got injuries which will make him to lead his life by adjusting with the said injuries.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs. 40,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
PW2 stated that the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery in the form of implant removal.
But he has not produced any estimation.
Hence, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
I) LOSS OF MARRIAGE PROSPECTS :
The PW.1/ petitioner had contended that due to the injuries sustained by him, he is unable to find a fiance for marriage.
The evidence of doctor witness goes to show that the petitioner has got severe permanent disabilities and also due to the crush injury he has got severe visible marks in his left leg.
The photographs produced at the time of arguments shows the present condition of the petitioner.
The petitioner is of 20 yeas old and his better life is yet to come.

Obviously the matrimonial prospects of the victim/petitioner who suffered grievous Aravind M vs Sunstar Logistics Pvt Ltd on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6476587/
7 accidental injuries, would also be severely affected.

sentences.text: To put it differently the marital prospects of the petitioner are bleak.
If a person chooses to be a bachelor throughout the life, it is their wish.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs. 25,53,000/-
(Rupees Twenty five lakhs fifty three thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount 50% shall be released to petitioner, on his proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in his name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
The respondents have not led any rebuttal evidence.
19. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 05.10.2024 which was caused by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.HR-55-AR- 4649 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.12,32,200/- by excluding the amount paid by the Personal Health Insurance.
If a person chooses to be a bachelor throughout the life, it is their wish.
Whereas if a person is compelled to remain so because of an unfortunate accident then that will lead to mental agony.
In this regard in the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2021 ACJ 2645 in the case of Divisional Manager, National Insurance, Company V/s Akash and another wherein it is held for loss of marriage prospects to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/-.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs. 25,53,000/-
(Rupees Twenty five lakhs fifty three thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of awarded amount 50% shall be released to petitioner, on his proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in his name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
